b2-89.title: The dance competition
b2-89.story: Anna and Max entered a dance competition at the youth center in Kyiv. They had practiced their [[salsa]] for weeks, but on the day, Max was so nervous that his hands were shaking. The first couple performed a dramatic [[tango]], and the crowd went wild. Next came a lively [[samba]] by two girls in bright costumes with feathers. Before Anna and Max's turn, Lisa sang a [[duet]] with her cousin, and Ira played a short violin [[solo]]. Then a jazz [[trio]] from the music school played while the judges took notes. When the music finally started, Anna and Max forgot their fears and danced better than ever. They didn't win first place, but the judges called them "the happiest [[duo]] of the night."

b2-90.title: The school concert
b2-90.story: Taras's school was preparing for its spring concert, and the music room was full of noise. One boy was practicing the [[banjo]], while two girls tried to play the [[trombone]] without laughing. Taras had chosen the [[ukulele]] because it was small and easy to carry. His classmate Dan, on the other hand, could barely lift his huge [[tuba]]. At the final rehearsal, the teacher asked Max, who was helping out, to play [[bass]] for the band. Halfway through the first song, one of Taras's strings broke with a loud noise. Everyone froze, and Taras turned bright red. "Well, that was a total [[fail]]," he joked, and the whole room burst out laughing. Max lent him a spare string, and on the night of the concert, everything went perfectly.

b2-91.title: A night at the ballet
b2-91.story: For Grandma's birthday, the family bought tickets to the [[ballet]] at the opera house in Kyiv. Anna had wanted to see a [[musical]] instead, but Grandma had dreamed about this evening for months. Before the show, a well-known [[tenor]] sang two short songs, and Grandpa whispered that his voice gave him goosebumps. Then the [[maestro]] raised his hand, and the orchestra began to play. The lead [[ballerina]] seemed to float across the stage like a feather. During the break, Anna read in the program that the theater's [[repertoire]] included over thirty performances this season. She also noticed that a famous piano [[sonata]] would be performed there next week. At home, Grandma was so moved that she wrote a [[sonnet]] about the evening and read it aloud at dinner. Even Anna had to admit that it was a perfect night.

b2-92.title: At the art exhibition
b2-92.story: On Saturday, Anna and Sofia went to an art exhibition in a glass [[pavilion]] in the city park. Outside, a young artist was finishing a giant [[mural]] of sunflowers on a wall. Inside, a [[sculptor]] was showing small figures made from old bicycle parts. Sofia's favorite room was full of drawings by an [[illustrator]] who works on children's books. Anna loved a corner with [[retro]] posters that looked like they came straight from the seventies. While they were looking at them, a serious man with a notebook stopped next to them. He turned out to be an [[art critic]] writing a review for a local magazine. He asked the girls which piece they liked best, and Sofia pointed to a drawing of a sleepy cat. A week later, Anna found the review online, and it quoted "a young visitor" who loved the cat.

b2-93.title: Beats at the club
b2-93.story: For Lisa's eighteenth birthday, the friends went to a small club near the river. The DJ started the night with a smooth [[mix]] of old soul and [[R&B]] hits. Later, the music changed to relaxed [[reggae]], and Ira tried to teach Max how to move to the beat. Around midnight, the lights turned blue and loud [[techno]] filled the room. Then the DJ surprised everyone with a [[remix]] of Lisa's favorite song from her childhood. Max, who never dances, jumped onto the small stage and performed a funny [[freestyle]] rap about Lisa. Everyone cheered, and Lisa laughed so hard that she nearly cried. It was, she said, the best birthday she had ever had.

b2-94.title: The punk years
b2-94.story: While cleaning the attic, Anna found a box of old photos and cassette tapes. "That's me at sixteen," laughed her dad, pointing to a boy with spiky green hair. Back then, he listened to nothing but [[punk]] and dreamed of becoming a famous [[rocker]]. He even started a [[punk rock]] band with two friends from his street. Mama, on the other hand, used to be a [[goth]] who wore only black clothes and dark lipstick. Then Grandma showed them a photo of herself as a young [[hippie]] with flowers in her hair. Taras couldn't stop laughing, especially when he heard that Grandpa had loved [[heavy metal]]. That evening, the whole family played the old tapes and danced around the living room.

b2-95.title: Casino night at home
b2-95.story: For Sofia's birthday, Max turned their living room into a pretend [[casino]] for one night. Nobody used real money, because Max believed that [[gambling]] was a terrible way to lose your savings. Instead, every guest got a bag of chocolate coins at the door. Lisa and Ira sat down at the card table and tried to learn [[poker]] from Max's dad. Anna preferred [[blackjack]] because the rules were easier to understand. In one game, the [[joker]] could replace any card, and Taras kept forgetting what that meant. In the corner, an old [[pinball]] machine that Dad had repaired was beeping and flashing all evening. At the end of the night, Sofia hit the [[jackpot]] and won the biggest box of chocolates.

b2-96.title: A weekend of shows
b2-96.story: Anna wanted to give her little brother Taras the best weekend of his school break. On Friday evening, they watched an amazing [[light show]] on the old buildings by the river. On Saturday morning, they joined the crowds at a colorful [[parade]] through the city center. In the afternoon, they went to an [[ice show]], where skaters dressed as cartoon characters spun across the rink. Afterwards, they warmed up with hot chocolate at a cozy [[art cafe]] full of paintings and old lamps. The cafe also sold [[handmade]] gifts, and Taras bought a tiny painted [[matryoshka]] for Grandma. At the next table, a woman was teaching kids to fold paper cranes, and Taras spent an hour learning [[origami]]. On Sunday night, the weekend ended with a [[fire show]] on the beach, and Taras said it was the best weekend ever.
